promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: New right knee pain on Sunday's long run changes the plan: skip the tempo, keep every run easy and flat this week, and get the knee looked at by a sports physio before we add intensity back in.

flags.detail: planned 13 mi easy, ran 9 mi and walked the last half mile with sharp outer-knee pain on downhills.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
1. I can't tell you what it is, and I won't guess from here: pain on the outside of the knee that gets worse on downhills and lingers on stairs is worth a visit to a sports physio or sports-medicine doctor this week. Ask them for a return-to-run plan and whether strength work for hips and glutes would help. In the meantime treat it as real, not something to run through.

2. No tempo on Wednesday. We swap it for easy cross-training or a short easy run on a flat route, and we also shrink the long run. If the knee is pain-free all week we can bring intensity back the week after, guided by what the physio says.

new.analysis:
## What I'm reading from the week

You followed the plan right up to Sunday, and that is the one I want to flag. Tue, Wed tempo, Thu and Sat all landed as written, with the tempo reps clean at 7:59/mi and no fade. Then the long run turned at mile 7 and you did the right thing by walking it in.

The pattern matters more than the single run. This is new pain in a body that has been healthy for two years, it got worse through the run, it was worst on downhills, and it was still there on stairs the next day. That is why we pause the hard work rather than push on and hope.

## Why this week looks the way it does

I am turning this into your down week, two weeks earlier than planned. Volume drops to around 19 miles, all easy, all flat where you can manage it, with a cross-train swap on Wednesday to keep aerobic time without the pounding of a tempo. The long run shrinks to 8 miles on a flat loop, with permission to stop if the knee speaks up.

We still have 10 weeks to the marathon, which is enough runway. One quiet week now, a physio visit, and we can rebuild the long run and bring the tempo back the week after. If the knee is unhappy on Tue or Wed, cut the run short and message me rather than grind through.

## What to watch during the runs

Flat ground, no camber if you can help it, and ease off any downhill. If a run starts fine and the pain shows up, that is your signal to walk home, not to push to the planned distance. Keep logging the pain score honestly: it is the single most useful number this week.

Record whether you see a sports physio or doctor this week, and share any return-to-run guidance they give.
Consider adding 2 short hip and glute strength sessions per week once cleared, if the clinician agrees.

safetyCallouts.title: See a sports physio about the right knee.
safetyCallouts.body: New lateral knee pain that sharpens on downhills and aches on stairs the day after is worth a professional look before you push mileage or add speed. Stop a run if the pain comes back sharply, gets worse mile to mile, or changes how you walk. Ice and gentle movement are fine; let the clinician guide any specific treatment or strength work.
